confidence.reason.lowCoverage: Not enough answers for a reliable reading
confidence.reason.partialCloseCall: In some areas the top two are close
ism.art.baroque.desc: Characterized by grandeur, dynamism, drama, and elaborate ornamentation.
ism.art.classicism.desc: Admires the harmony, order, and rational beauty of ancient Greece and Rome.
ism.art.dadaism.desc: Anti-art, anti-reason, anti-tradition — challenges definition through absurdity and chaos.
ism.art.expressionism.desc: Distorts reality to express inner emotions and subjective feelings.
ism.art.functionalism.desc: Form follows function — practicality and efficiency determine design.
ism.art.impressionism.desc: Captures fleeting light and sensory impressions, emphasizing subjective experience.
ism.art.minimalism.desc: Reduces to essential elements, removing ornamentation, pursuing pure form.
ism.art.naturalism.desc: Faithfully reproduces nature and reality, emphasizing objective observation.
ism.art.realism.desc: Depicts life and the world objectively and truthfully, without idealization.
ism.art.romanticism.desc: Emphasizes emotion, imagination, nature, and individual expression.
ism.art.surrealism.desc: Unleashes the subconscious through dreamlike, absurd imagery, breaking rational constraints.
ism.art.symbolism.desc: Expresses inner spiritual worlds through symbols, metaphors, and mystical imagery.
ism.cult.animalliberation.desc: Animals deserve equal rights and freedom from human exploitation.
ism.cult.backtonature.desc: Returns to a simple, natural lifestyle, distancing from modern civilization.
ism.cult.bohemianism.desc: A free-spirited, unconventional life pursuing art and spiritual experiences.
ism.cult.collectivism.desc: Group goals and welfare take priority over individual interests and desires.
ism.cult.consumerism.desc: Achieves satisfaction and identity through continuous consumption.
ism.cult.ecologism.desc: Prioritizes the overall health of ecosystems; humans are part of nature.
ism.cult.environmentalism.desc: Protects the natural environment and promotes sustainable lifestyles.
ism.cult.futurism.desc: Embraces the future, speed, technology, and change while rejecting tradition.
ism.cult.individualism.desc: Individual independence and self-realization take precedence over collective goals.
ism.cult.luddism.desc: Opposes or warns against new technologies, citing job loss and loss of humanity.
ism.cult.materialism.desc: Material wealth and consumption are the primary markers of happiness and success.
ism.cult.minimalism.desc: Deliberately owning less and keeping only what is genuinely needed.
ism.cult.modernism.desc: Celebrates reason, progress, innovation, and universal standards.
ism.cult.spiritualism.desc: Inner spiritual growth is more important than material pursuits.
ism.cult.technicism.desc: Technology is the primary force for solving human problems and driving progress.
ism.cult.technooptimism.desc: Believes technological advances will bring a brighter future.
ism.cult.technopessimism.desc: Warns of technology's negative consequences such as alienation, surveillance, and environmental damage.
ism.cult.traditionalism.desc: Respects and preserves historically inherited culture, institutions, and values.
ism.cult.vegetarianism.desc: Avoids animal products for moral, health, or environmental reasons.
ism.econ.capitalism.desc: Private ownership of the means of production, market-driven resource allocation, profit-seeking.
ism.econ.cooperativism.desc: Workers or consumers cooperatively own and operate enterprises.
ism.econ.distributism.desc: Broadly disperses property ownership, opposing concentration of wealth.
ism.econ.georgism.desc: Replaces other taxes with land value tax; land should be socially owned.
ism.econ.interventionism.desc: Government should actively intervene in the economy to correct market failures.
ism.econ.keynesianism.desc: Manages aggregate demand through government spending and fiscal policy to stabilize the economy.
ism.econ.laissezfaire.desc: Government does not intervene in the economy; the market regulates itself.
ism.econ.marketeconomy.desc: Resources are allocated through markets, with government providing the basic framework.
ism.econ.mercantilism.desc: Nations strengthen themselves through trade surpluses and accumulation of wealth.
ism.econ.mixedeconomy.desc: Combines market mechanisms with government intervention, balancing efficiency and fairness.
ism.econ.monetarism.desc: Controlling the money supply is the primary means of stabilizing the economy.
ism.econ.mutualism.desc: Organizes the economy through cooperation and mutual exchange rather than competition.
ism.econ.plannedeconomy.desc: Resources and production are allocated by state planning rather than markets.
ism.econ.schumpeterianism.desc: Innovation and creative destruction are the core drivers of economic development.
ism.econ.supplyside.desc: Stimulates production through tax cuts and deregulation, driving economic growth.
ism.ethi.altruism.desc: People should selflessly care for the welfare of others, even at personal sacrifice.
ism.ethi.asceticism.desc: Achieves spiritual or moral perfection through self-denial and restraint of desires.
ism.ethi.careethics.desc: The core of morality lies in relationships, care, and compassion.
ism.ethi.consequentialism.desc: Rightness or wrongness of actions depends solely on their outcomes.
ism.ethi.deontology.desc: Actions are morally right if they conform to duty, regardless of consequences.
ism.ethi.egoism.desc: Self-interest should be the ultimate goal of action.
ism.ethi.emotivism.desc: Moral judgments express emotions and attitudes rather than facts.
ism.ethi.hedonism.desc: Pleasure and joy are life's highest goals and intrinsic values.
ism.ethi.moralabsolutism.desc: There are universal, unchanging moral principles applicable to all cultures.
ism.ethi.moralnihilism.desc: Objective morality does not exist; moral statements have no truth value.
ism.ethi.moralrelativism.desc: Moral judgments vary by culture, individual, or context; no universal standards exist.
ism.ethi.religiousethics.desc: Moral principles derive from religious faith and divine commandments.
ism.ethi.secularism.desc: Public life and morality should not depend on religion but be based on reason.
ism.ethi.utilitarianism.desc: The greatest happiness for the greatest number is the standard of morality.
ism.ethi.virtueethics.desc: Focuses on cultivating virtues and character, becoming a virtuous person.
ism.phil.absolutism.desc: There exist universal, unchanging truths, moral principles, or value standards.
ism.phil.absurdism.desc: Acknowledges the conflict between seeking meaning and the meaninglessness of the universe, yet chooses to embrace life.
ism.phil.cynicism.desc: Maintains a pervasive distrust and mockery of social norms and others' motives.
ism.phil.deconstruction.desc: Dissolves fixed meanings and binary oppositions, revealing internal contradictions in texts.
ism.phil.determinism.desc: All events are determined by prior causes; free will is an illusion.
ism.phil.dialectics.desc: Understands change and development through the unity of contradictions.
ism.phil.empiricism.desc: All knowledge derives from sensory experience, rejecting innate ideas.
ism.phil.epicureanism.desc: Pursues moderate pleasure and the absence of pain to achieve tranquility of mind.
ism.phil.existentialism.desc: Emphasizes individual existence, freedom, and choice — existence precedes essence.
ism.phil.freewill.desc: Human beings possess the genuine ability to make choices under given conditions.
ism.phil.humanism.desc: Centers on human value, dignity, and reason.
ism.phil.idealism.desc: Mind or spirit is the fundamental substance of reality; matter is its product or appearance.
ism.phil.logicalpositivism.desc: Only statements that are mathematical, logical, or verifiable are meaningful.
ism.phil.materialism.desc: Matter is the fundamental substance of reality; consciousness is a product of matter.
ism.phil.naturalism.desc: Holds that nature is the whole of reality and that nothing supernatural exists.
ism.phil.nihilism.desc: Asserts that life lacks objective meaning, purpose, or intrinsic value.
ism.phil.objectivism.desc: Champions reason, individualism, and laissez-faire capitalism.
ism.phil.optimism.desc: Believes the world is moving toward improvement and the future is hopeful.
ism.phil.pessimism.desc: Views life as inherently painful — to exist is to suffer.
ism.phil.phenomenology.desc: Returns to the things themselves, describing the essential structures of conscious experience.
ism.phil.positivism.desc: Only verifiable scientific knowledge constitutes authentic knowledge.
ism.phil.postmodernism.desc: Questions grand narratives, universal truths, and objective knowledge.
ism.phil.pragmaticrationalism.desc: Combines rational analysis with practical effects to guide action.
ism.phil.pragmatism.desc: Truth is defined by its practical effects and applications.
ism.phil.rationalism.desc: Reason is the primary source of knowledge, superior to sensory experience.
ism.phil.relativism.desc: Truth, morality, or values are relative to culture, individual, or context.
ism.phil.skepticism.desc: Systematically questions the possibility of certain knowledge.
ism.phil.stoicism.desc: Pursues inner peace and virtue through rational control of emotions.
ism.phil.structuralism.desc: Emphasizes that deep structures determine phenomena; individuals are constrained by systems.
ism.phil.transcendentalism.desc: Believes in the possibility of directly grasping ultimate reality beyond sense and reason.
ism.phil.voluntarism.desc: The will to power is the fundamental drive of life, pursuing self-overcoming.
ism.poli.anarchism.desc: Opposes all coercive hierarchies and authority, including the state.
ism.poli.anticolonialism.desc: Opposes colonial rule, striving for national independence and self-determination.
ism.poli.authoritarianism.desc: Emphasizes obedience to authority, restricting individual freedom in exchange for order and security.
ism.poli.centrism.desc: Seeks balance between left and right on the political spectrum.
ism.poli.colonialism.desc: Powerful nations control and exploit other regions, seen as an oppressive ideology.
ism.poli.communism.desc: Abolishes private property, realizing a classless society of "from each according to ability, to each according to need."
ism.poli.communitarianism.desc: Emphasizes community values and social responsibilities, criticizing excessive individualism.
ism.poli.conservatism.desc: Upholds traditional institutions, moral order, and gradual change.
ism.poli.cosmopolitanism.desc: All people belong to a single global community, transcending geographic and cultural boundaries.
ism.poli.democracy.desc: Sovereignty resides in the people, exercised through elections and participation.
ism.poli.egalitarianism.desc: Advocates for equality of social, economic, and political conditions for all people.
ism.poli.elitism.desc: Society should be led by the most capable and talented minority.
ism.poli.federalism.desc: Supports a decentralized system combining local autonomy with central authority.
ism.poli.internationalism.desc: Promotes transnational cooperation and global solidarity beyond national boundaries.
ism.poli.isolationism.desc: Avoids involvement in foreign affairs, focusing on domestic development.
ism.poli.liberalism.desc: Emphasizes individual freedom, rights protection, limited government, and rule of law.
ism.poli.libertarianism.desc: Advocates for minimal government or even anarchy, maximizing individual and market freedom.
ism.poli.moderatism.desc: Avoids extremes, seeking compromise and gradual reform.
ism.poli.nationalism.desc: Centers on national interests, emphasizing national identity and sovereignty.
ism.poli.neoliberalism.desc: Champions free markets, privatization, deregulation, and globalization.
ism.poli.patriotism.desc: Love for one's country, supporting its interests and values.
ism.poli.populism.desc: Claims to represent ordinary people against elites and the establishment.
ism.poli.progressivism.desc: Believes in continuous social reform to advance equality and justice.
ism.poli.radicalism.desc: Advocates for fundamental changes to existing social, political, or economic structures.
ism.poli.republicanism.desc: Emphasizes civic virtue, public good, and checks and balances, opposing hereditary power.
ism.poli.separatism.desc: Advocates for a group to secede from an existing state and establish an independent nation.
ism.poli.socialdemocracy.desc: Achieves social justice and a welfare state through democratic means within a capitalist framework.
ism.poli.socialism.desc: Advocates public ownership of the means of production, economic equality, and social welfare.
ism.poli.thirdway.desc: A middle path between traditional socialism and neoliberalism.
mbti.dim.energy.desc: The direction your energy flows: Extraversion (E) versus Introversion (I)
mbti.dim.identity.desc: How you appraise yourself under pressure: Assertive (A) versus Turbulent (T)
mbti.dim.mind.desc: How you take in information: Sensing (S) versus Intuition (N)
mbti.dim.nature.desc: How you process information to decide: Thinking (T) versus Feeling (F)
mbti.dim.tactics.desc: How you engage with the world around you: Judging (J) versus Perceiving (P)
mbti.tiebreak.energy.1: On a free evening, you would rather be with a group of people.
mbti.tiebreak.energy.2: On a free evening, you would rather be on your own.
mbti.tiebreak.energy.q: This trait came out even. Which of these is more like you?
mbti.tiebreak.identity.1: After a mistake, you would rather move on.
mbti.tiebreak.identity.2: After a mistake, you would rather keep going over it.
mbti.tiebreak.identity.q: This trait came out even. Which of these is more like you?
mbti.tiebreak.mind.1: After a film, you would rather discuss what it is trying to say.
mbti.tiebreak.mind.2: After a film, you would rather discuss what happens in it.
mbti.tiebreak.mind.q: This trait came out even. Which of these is more like you?
mbti.tiebreak.nature.1: When a friend brings you a problem, you would rather help them solve it.
mbti.tiebreak.nature.2: When a friend brings you a problem, you would rather comfort them first.
mbti.tiebreak.nature.q: This trait came out even. Which of these is more like you?
mbti.tiebreak.tactics.1: Before a trip, you would rather have the whole thing planned out.
mbti.tiebreak.tactics.2: Before a trip, you would rather figure it out as you go.
mbti.tiebreak.tactics.q: This trait came out even. Which of these is more like you?
mbti.type.ENFJ.desc: Protagonists are inspiring optimists, readily taking action to do what they feel is right.
mbti.type.ENFJ.name: Protagonist
mbti.type.ENFP.desc: Campaigners are enthusiastic, creative, and sociable free spirits, who can always find a reason to smile.
mbti.type.ENFP.name: Campaigner
mbti.type.ENTJ.desc: Commanders are bold, imaginative, and strong-willed, always finding a way – or making one.
mbti.type.ENTJ.name: Commander
mbti.type.ENTP.desc: Debaters are curious and flexible thinkers who cannot resist an intellectual challenge.
mbti.type.ENTP.name: Debater
mbti.type.ESFJ.desc: Consuls are very caring, social, community-minded people who are always eager to help.
mbti.type.ESFJ.name: Consul
mbti.type.ESFP.desc: Entertainers are spontaneous, energetic, and enthusiastic people – life is never boring around them.
mbti.type.ESFP.name: Entertainer
mbti.type.ESTJ.desc: Executives are excellent organizers, unsurpassed at managing things – or people.
mbti.type.ESTJ.name: Executive
mbti.type.ESTP.desc: Entrepreneurs are savvy, energetic, and very perceptive people who truly enjoy living on the edge.
mbti.type.ESTP.name: Entrepreneur
mbti.type.INFJ.desc: Advocates are quiet visionaries, often serving as inspiring and tireless idealists.
mbti.type.INFJ.name: Advocate
mbti.type.INFP.desc: Mediators are poetic, kind, and altruistic people, always eager to help a good cause.
mbti.type.INFP.name: Mediator
mbti.type.INTJ.desc: Architects are imaginative and strategic thinkers, with a plan for everything.
mbti.type.INTJ.name: Architect
mbti.type.INTP.desc: Logicians are innovative inventors with an unquenchable thirst for knowledge.
mbti.type.INTP.name: Logician
mbti.type.ISFJ.desc: Defenders are very dedicated and warm protectors, always ready to defend their loved ones.
mbti.type.ISFJ.name: Defender
mbti.type.ISFP.desc: Adventurers are flexible and charming, always ready to explore and experience something new.
mbti.type.ISFP.name: Adventurer
mbti.type.ISTJ.desc: Logisticians are practical and fact-minded individuals, whose reliability cannot be doubted.
mbti.type.ISTJ.name: Logistician
mbti.type.ISTP.desc: Virtuosos are innovative and practical experimenters, masters of all kinds of tools.
mbti.type.ISTP.name: Virtuoso
q.ideo.v1.001: Major national decisions must be made swiftly by the central government; leaving them to localities to handle separately only causes trouble.
q.ideo.v1.002: Public decisions must be answerable to ordinary people; whoever makes a decision must explain the reasons for it.
q.ideo.v1.003: The interests of our own citizens must come first; that is the precondition for any political community to exist.
q.ideo.v1.004: National borders are historical accidents; I owe no less to strangers far away than to my own neighbours.
q.ideo.v1.005: Practices that have survived for centuries have their reasons; discarding them untested is a form of arrogance.
q.ideo.v1.006: Piecemeal adjustments cannot solve fundamental problems; the whole structure has to be torn down and rebuilt.
q.ideo.v1.007: Prices should be set by supply and demand; no central authority can ever hold enough information to replace them.
q.ideo.v1.008: Resources essential to the national livelihood must be planned centrally; leaving them to the market will certainly spin out of control.
q.ideo.v1.009: As long as the starting line is fair and the rules are the same for everyone, unequal outcomes are acceptable.
q.ideo.v1.010: Unemployment, illness and old age can happen to anyone; society as a whole must catch people when they fall.
q.ideo.v1.011: My life is mine to decide; other people's expectations are not a reason for anything.
q.ideo.v1.012: Apart from the community an individual is nothing; when it comes down to it, the individual should give way.
q.ideo.v1.013: Being able to own more and experience more is a good thing in itself.
q.ideo.v1.014: The fewer things I own the freer I am; everything surplus is a burden.
q.ideo.v1.015: Nature is not a warehouse of resources; human needs do not automatically outweigh what ecosystems can bear.
q.ideo.v1.016: Nature exists for human use; human welfare is the only measure that counts.
q.ideo.v1.017: A person can make completely different choices in exactly the same situation; that is what makes them human.
q.ideo.v1.018: Every choice a person makes has causes behind it; what we call freedom is just causes we have not yet traced.
q.ideo.v1.019: Truly reliable knowledge comes from logical deduction; the senses deceive us.
q.ideo.v1.020: Any conclusion can be overturned; what matters is staying sceptical rather than rushing to a verdict.
q.ideo.v1.021: Some things must not be done no matter how good the outcome would be; that is the line.
q.ideo.v1.022: Right and wrong are judged by what actually results; motives and rules are secondary.
q.ideo.v1.023: A genuinely good work survives repeated viewing; what carries it is structure and proportion.
q.ideo.v1.024: Art exists to move people; anything safe and well-behaved is lifeless.
q.ideo.v1.025: When standards differ from place to place, it is the rule-followers who lose out.
q.ideo.v1.026: In a crisis, the more concentrated the decision-making, the faster the response.
q.ideo.v1.027: Localities should decide their own affairs; higher authorities should keep their hands off.
q.ideo.v1.028: Spreading power among as many hands as possible is safer than concentrating it in a few.
q.ideo.v1.029: The same policy producing different results in different places is not necessarily a bad thing.
q.ideo.v1.030: When a reform is to be rolled out nationally, someone eventually has to make the call.
q.ideo.v1.031: Governing is a professional job; leaving it to people who know what they are doing beats letting everyone have a say.
q.ideo.v1.032: Major decisions should not be settled by a momentary wave of emotional public opinion.
q.ideo.v1.033: Without media and auditors who can speak independently, accountability is just a phrase.
q.ideo.v1.034: A decision that no one can be held to account for will eventually turn into a bad decision.
q.ideo.v1.035: Letting the people who understand the matter best decide usually works out better.
q.ideo.v1.036: Having gone through the proper procedure does not mean the decision was right.
q.ideo.v1.037: Once the votes are counted the result should be carried out; it should not be overturned because a minority is unhappy.
q.ideo.v1.038: For a society to move forward, it has to go by what most people want.
q.ideo.v1.039: Majorities can oppress too; the rights of minorities and dissenters must be written in stone.
q.ideo.v1.040: Something most people agree on can still be something that should not be done.
q.ideo.v1.041: A proposal passing quickly does not mean it was thought through.
q.ideo.v1.042: Consensus is fine, but if you wait for everyone to nod, nothing ever gets done.
q.ideo.v1.043: The accents, the food, the look of a place keep changing. That is not a place losing itself; it is a place still alive.
q.ideo.v1.044: Where a person's cultural roots are is where their belonging is.
q.ideo.v1.045: I am a human being first and a citizen of some country second.
q.ideo.v1.046: Putting national interest above all humanity harms everyone in the long run.
q.ideo.v1.047: Every country's circumstances differ; copying another country's system rarely works.
q.ideo.v1.048: When the same thing happens in a different country, I feel exactly the same about it.
q.ideo.v1.049: People and cultures moving too fast erodes social trust; it needs to be moderated.
q.ideo.v1.050: A community has to have a shape of its own before it can talk about taking others in.
q.ideo.v1.051: The vitality that foreign cultures bring far outweighs the shock; they should be welcomed.
q.ideo.v1.052: My neighbourhood has accents from all over, and that makes me comfortable.
q.ideo.v1.053: Learning other people's language and technology does not mean giving up your own.
q.ideo.v1.054: Whether a culture survives ultimately depends on whether it has vitality of its own.
q.ideo.v1.055: Once a community has formed, it should not be broken up at will because one part wants out.
q.ideo.v1.056: Some things can never be put back together once separated, so it is better not to separate them.
q.ideo.v1.057: If a group does not want to stay, forcing them to only brings greater suffering.
q.ideo.v1.058: Deciding your own affairs is the same principle for a group as for an individual.
q.ideo.v1.059: Separation is costly and staying together has its price; you can only weigh the lesser evil.
q.ideo.v1.060: The lines on the map are drawn; the lines in people's hearts are not.
q.ideo.v1.061: Upheaval tends to bring unforeseen disaster; better to go one step at a time.
q.ideo.v1.062: Change the institutions too fast and people cannot keep up; a good thing turns into a bad one.
q.ideo.v1.063: Unless the old is torn down, the new can never be built.
q.ideo.v1.064: Some windows of opportunity last only a few years; miss them and they are gone for good.
q.ideo.v1.065: The pace of reform depends on conditions; there is no fixed rule.
q.ideo.v1.066: Waiting until conditions are fully ripe usually means never acting at all.
q.ideo.v1.067: Procedure is a nuisance, but what it protects is exactly the people who have no voice.
q.ideo.v1.068: The customs that go with the festivals are ones I would not skip a single one of.
q.ideo.v1.069: Tradition is often just the unreasonableness of the past; being old should not exempt it from question.
q.ideo.v1.070: How my grandparents did things is not a reason for how I should do them.
q.ideo.v1.071: The old way has its reasons and the new way has its own.
q.ideo.v1.072: Much of what is taken as self-evident turns out, in hindsight, to be the habit of one era.
q.ideo.v1.073: Improper means cannot be justified by good results.
q.ideo.v1.074: Not one step of the required procedure may be skipped, even when everyone knows the outcome.
q.ideo.v1.075: When the rules themselves produce injustice, going around them is necessary.
q.ideo.v1.076: If the outcome saves many lives, flaws in the procedure can be repaired afterwards.
q.ideo.v1.077: However detailed the rules, there are gaps; what matters is whether anyone enforces them seriously.
q.ideo.v1.078: Sticking to procedure in an emergency is itself a dereliction of duty.
q.ideo.v1.079: A factory will not put the waste it discharges on its own books; someone has to keep that account for everyone.
q.ideo.v1.080: What a thing is worth is for the buyer and the seller to work out between themselves.
q.ideo.v1.081: What to produce and how much should be arranged centrally by a planning body.
q.ideo.v1.082: Things that affect everyone’s livelihood must not be left to a profit-seeking market to decide.
q.ideo.v1.083: Prices rising and falling is not in itself a bad thing; it is how information travels.
q.ideo.v1.084: Once something is allocated purely by price, poor people can no longer get any of it.
q.ideo.v1.085: The less the government meddles, the more vitality the economy has.
q.ideo.v1.086: Government involvement distorts things; the best policy is to intervene as little as possible.
q.ideo.v1.087: Markets fail; the government has a duty to step in during slumps and monopolies.
q.ideo.v1.088: Some industries must be run by the government; handing them to private owners always causes problems.
q.ideo.v1.089: A central bank acting by pre-announced rules is more reliable than ad hoc decisions.
q.ideo.v1.090: Subsidising an industry is sometimes necessary, but subsidise it long enough and no one will walk on their own.
q.ideo.v1.091: Clear property rights are the precondition for prosperity; what is commonly owned tends to become no one’s responsibility.
q.ideo.v1.092: How I spend the money I earn is not something I need to report to anyone.
q.ideo.v1.093: When the key means of production are in private hands, genuine equality is impossible.
q.ideo.v1.094: Land and mineral resources should never have belonged to any individual in the first place.
q.ideo.v1.095: State ownership and private ownership each have their proper place.
q.ideo.v1.096: Shares dispersed among employees is not the same thing as outright private ownership.
q.ideo.v1.097: Getting everyone to the same starting line matters more than getting everyone to the finish line together.
q.ideo.v1.098: Income gaps are normal, as long as the gap was earned.
q.ideo.v1.099: Fair starting points are an illusion; without narrowing the outcome gap there is no equality to speak of.
q.ideo.v1.100: A society that allows some individuals to be richer than whole nations has a problem in itself.
q.ideo.v1.101: Looking at the income gap alone tells you nothing; what matters is whether people have a way upward.
q.ideo.v1.102: When people who try equally hard end up with different results, it is hard to call that fair.
q.ideo.v1.103: Letting the most capable win is what makes the whole better off.
q.ideo.v1.104: Competition makes people improve, and that holds in the marketplace as much as in the classroom.
q.ideo.v1.105: Handing resources to whoever wins the competition only magnifies injustice.
q.ideo.v1.106: People should first be helping each other along, not racing to see who is fastest.
q.ideo.v1.107: Competition is what creates drive, but winner-takes-all rules deserve scrutiny.
q.ideo.v1.108: Cooperatives and mutual aid societies run on voluntariness, not on benefits handed out by the state.
q.ideo.v1.109: You are responsible for your own choices; cushioning people too much breeds dependence.
q.ideo.v1.110: How a person ends up depends mostly on how hard they work.
q.ideo.v1.111: How a society treats its weakest members is the mark of whether it is civilised.
q.ideo.v1.112: Healthcare and education should not depend on how much money is in your pocket.
q.ideo.v1.113: A safety net is right, but not one that cushions people until no one wants to work.
q.ideo.v1.114: Some people end up where they are, and it really is not because they did not try hard enough.
q.ideo.v1.115: The collective exists for the individual; it cannot turn around and demand the individual sacrifice for it.
q.ideo.v1.116: If I do not fight for my own interests, no one else will.
q.ideo.v1.117: A person’s worth is, in the end, realised within the group they belong to.
q.ideo.v1.118: When something big comes up, thinking “we” before “me” is basic upbringing.
q.ideo.v1.119: The individual and the collective are not always opposed; very often they are the same thing.
q.ideo.v1.120: When someone says “for everyone’s good”, there is usually someone making decisions on others’ behalf.
q.ideo.v1.121: How a person lives is something only they are qualified to decide.
q.ideo.v1.122: I do not much care what other people think of my choices.
q.ideo.v1.123: People carry responsibilities to family and community that cannot be shrugged off, and those decide how one should live.
q.ideo.v1.124: Knowing your place in the family and the group is what lets a person feel settled.
q.ideo.v1.125: Independence and reliance are not either-or; everyone needs others at some point.
q.ideo.v1.126: Teaching a child early that “you only need to be yourself” is not necessarily a good thing.
q.ideo.v1.127: Look after yourself first and you will have something left for others; self-interest is not shameful.
q.ideo.v1.128: Helping others is a kindness; not helping is no wrongdoing.
q.ideo.v1.129: The suffering of others is not fundamentally different from my own and should be weighed the same.
q.ideo.v1.130: Seeing someone suffer and feeling nothing is wrong in itself.
q.ideo.v1.131: Everyone has a bit of self-interest; that is entirely normal.
q.ideo.v1.132: When it is a small thing you can do in passing, there is nothing to hesitate about.
q.ideo.v1.133: Living standards, income and achievement are the solid measures of whether life is going well.
q.ideo.v1.134: Making a good life for yourself is the most practical thing there is.
q.ideo.v1.135: Once external conditions improve past a certain point they stop meaning anything; what matters is the inner life.
q.ideo.v1.136: Whether a person deserves respect has nothing to do with their income or their show.
q.ideo.v1.137: Is there anything wrong with wanting life to be a bit more comfortable?
q.ideo.v1.138: Money spent on other people leaves me steadier than money spent on myself.
q.ideo.v1.139: Money in hand is what keeps you calm; everything else can wait.
q.ideo.v1.140: Being able to buy whatever you want is an important kind of freedom.
q.ideo.v1.141: Time spent on what you actually like is worth more than a bigger flat.
q.ideo.v1.142: A home stuffed with things nobody uses just makes a person tired.
q.ideo.v1.143: Whether to buy more or less depends on what is needed at the time.
q.ideo.v1.144: Before buying, think about whether it is really needed.
q.ideo.v1.145: Life is short; when you can be happy, you should be.
q.ideo.v1.146: Eat what you feel like eating; do not make things hard for yourself.
q.ideo.v1.147: Indulging desire only puts you under its control; restraint is what freedom means.
q.ideo.v1.148: Appetite can and should be held in check.
q.ideo.v1.149: After a hard day, a good meal in the evening is no crime.
q.ideo.v1.150: Finish what needs doing first, then think about enjoying yourself.
q.ideo.v1.151: For humanity’s own long-term good, we still have to give way to nature.
q.ideo.v1.152: Before developing anything, ask first whether the ecosystem can bear it.
q.ideo.v1.153: Some things cannot be called back once they are out, so think a few more steps before letting them out.
q.ideo.v1.154: Leaving resources in the ground is worse than using them to improve life.
q.ideo.v1.155: Development and protection are not necessarily an either-or.
q.ideo.v1.156: When you are poor, you cannot afford to talk about protection.
q.ideo.v1.157: Species and ecosystems have value independent of human beings.
q.ideo.v1.158: Even a river nobody uses has a reason to exist.
q.ideo.v1.159: Protecting the environment is ultimately about people living better.
q.ideo.v1.160: Saying nature has rights is a kind of anthropomorphism.
q.ideo.v1.161: The relationship between humans and other species deserves rethinking.
q.ideo.v1.162: Whatever people build, people will find a way to manage.
q.ideo.v1.163: Animals feel pain and fear as we do; killing them for appetite is unjustified.
q.ideo.v1.164: Eating meat is itself something worth reflecting on.
q.ideo.v1.165: Animals may be used by humans, as long as no unnecessary suffering is caused.
q.ideo.v1.166: Elevating animals to the same standing as people misses the point.
q.ideo.v1.167: How a society treats animals says something about what it is like.
q.ideo.v1.168: Better conditions on farms would be welcome, but there is no need to make a crusade of it.
q.ideo.v1.169: Every new technology creates risks we do not yet understand.
q.ideo.v1.170: If you can do without it, do without it; slower is no bad thing.
q.ideo.v1.171: The problems technology creates will ultimately be solved by better technology.
q.ideo.v1.172: A new technology should be adopted as soon as it appears; waiting for others to try it first wastes the opportunity.
q.ideo.v1.173: Whether to adopt a new technology depends on what it solves and what it brings with it.
q.ideo.v1.174: A tool is a tool; you just use it.
q.ideo.v1.175: So-called mental phenomena can ultimately all be reduced to material processes.
q.ideo.v1.176: A human being is a biological organism; there is nothing mysterious about it.
q.ideo.v1.177: Consciousness is not a by-product of matter; it is the more fundamental thing.
q.ideo.v1.178: Treating everything as matter leaves out the part that matters most.
q.ideo.v1.179: The question of what the world is made of may be the wrong question to ask.
q.ideo.v1.180: Some things science cannot explain, and there is no need to force an explanation.
q.ideo.v1.181: No instrument can measure what pain feels like, and yet it is more certain than any measurement.
q.ideo.v1.182: Whatever choice a person makes, they must bear the consequences of it.
q.ideo.v1.183: Which options a person can even think of is already framed by where they came from.
q.ideo.v1.184: Many people’s circumstances were not chosen by them; blaming them entirely is unfair.
q.ideo.v1.185: Whether we are free may depend on which level you are asking about.
q.ideo.v1.186: People are shaped by their environment far more than they realise.
q.ideo.v1.187: Life has a purpose of its own; we simply have to find it.
q.ideo.v1.188: Meaning is hidden in tradition; those before us have already walked this road.
q.ideo.v1.189: The universe supplies no meaning; meaning can only be made by oneself, or there is none at all.
q.ideo.v1.190: Meaning is something you give yourself, so no one else gets to dictate what it should be.
q.ideo.v1.191: Some live by faith and some make their own meaning; both can last a lifetime.
q.ideo.v1.192: Stop asking what you are living for; just live the days in front of you well.
q.ideo.v1.193: Data does not speak for itself; you need a theory first to know what to look at.
q.ideo.v1.194: I will only believe something if it can be derived from first principles.
q.ideo.v1.195: All knowledge ultimately comes back to observation and experiment; deduction without experience just spins in place.
q.ideo.v1.196: However neatly the argument is made in a book, it is worth less than having seen the thing once myself.
q.ideo.v1.197: Thinking alone and looking alone are probably both insufficient.
q.ideo.v1.198: The hands understand before the head does; a lot of things are figured out by doing them.
q.ideo.v1.199: With the right method you can reach firm conclusions that stand up to testing.
q.ideo.v1.200: If something cannot be stated clearly, it is usually because it has not been thought through.
q.ideo.v1.201: What I am certain of today I will mostly have changed my mind about in a few years.
q.ideo.v1.202: The more assertively something is claimed, the more it deserves suspicion.
q.ideo.v1.203: In some fields certainty is attainable; in others only an approximation is.
q.ideo.v1.204: Admitting you do not know beats pretending that you do.
q.ideo.v1.205: The same question should have the same correct answer everywhere.
q.ideo.v1.206: Mathematics and physics work the same way in China as in Europe.
q.ideo.v1.207: What we call truth is often just one perspective, and it stops holding in another setting.
q.ideo.v1.208: The same principle means something different in a different culture.
q.ideo.v1.209: Some standards hold everywhere; others depend on the place.
q.ideo.v1.210: Who is right and who is wrong often depends on where you are standing.
q.ideo.v1.211: Doing something one should not do is not made right by the outcome happening to be good.
q.ideo.v1.212: To judge an action, look first at whether it conforms to the rules, not at what it brought about.
q.ideo.v1.213: As long as everyone ends up better off, some things along the way can be done.
q.ideo.v1.214: Good intentions that fail to get anything done amount to nothing.
q.ideo.v1.215: Whether motive or outcome should weigh more depends on what the case actually is.
q.ideo.v1.216: A moral judgment that pays no attention at all to consequences is too cold to be human.
q.ideo.v1.217: Morality is first of all holding the line; without that there is no point talking about character.
q.ideo.v1.218: Laying the rules out clearly is more reliable than hoping everyone will be conscientious.
q.ideo.v1.219: Someone who only keeps the rules can be quite cold; what matters is the kind of person you become.
q.ideo.v1.220: What a person is matters more fundamentally than what they have done.
q.ideo.v1.221: Rules and character both matter; it is hard to say which comes first.
q.ideo.v1.222: The places that insist most on rules are often the least humane.
q.ideo.v1.223: Some things are wrong in every era and every culture, without exception.
q.ideo.v1.224: Right is right and wrong is wrong; it does not change because everyone does it.
q.ideo.v1.225: Moral standards grow out of particular societies; one set should not be used to judge another.
q.ideo.v1.226: Each era has its own morality; there is no such thing as progress or decline in it.
q.ideo.v1.227: On fundamental matters there is nothing to negotiate; on small ones people live as they see fit.
q.ideo.v1.228: The same thing was seen quite differently twenty years ago and now.
q.ideo.v1.229: Once the camera arrived, painting no longer had to compete over which could look more like the thing.
q.ideo.v1.230: In anything that rewards repeated looking, the details are all placed just right.
q.ideo.v1.231: If a work cannot move you at all, perfect technique is of no use.
q.ideo.v1.232: Chaos, conflict, imbalance — these are exactly where art has the most power.
q.ideo.v1.233: Order and tension are both present in anything good.
q.ideo.v1.234: Comfortable to look at and striking to look at are two different kinds of good.
q.ideo.v1.235: The value of a work lies in how accurately it captures the real.
q.ideo.v1.236: Whether it looks like the thing is still a basic skill of the craft.
q.ideo.v1.237: Art does not have to resemble anything; form and colour can speak for themselves.
q.ideo.v1.238: Copying reality down is called documentation, not creation.
q.ideo.v1.239: Abstract and figurative each have their merits.
q.ideo.v1.240: Whether it can be understood should not be the standard for judging a work.
q.ideo.v1.241: Classical works have already shown what good looks like; learn that before talking about innovation.
q.ideo.v1.242: Rules that took centuries of trial to settle should not be thrown away lightly.
q.ideo.v1.243: Art moves forward by smashing the rules of the previous generation.
q.ideo.v1.244: A craft that only talks about transmission will stiffen before long.
q.ideo.v1.245: Learning tradition and making something new are not actually in conflict.
q.ideo.v1.246: Every generation finds the previous generation’s taste dated.
q.ideo.v1.247: Whether a minority keeps its rights should not be put to a majority vote.
q.ideo.v1.248: What you live for is a question with no standard answer.

q.ipip.20: Am not interested in abstract ideas.

q.ipip.28: Often forget to put things back in their proper place.
q.ipip.30: Do not have a good imagination.

q.ipip.32: Am not really interested in others.
q.ipip.36: Don't like to draw attention to myself.

q.mbti.16p.002: Complex and novel ideas excite you more than simple and straightforward ones.
q.mbti.16p.003: You usually feel more persuaded by what resonates emotionally with you than by factual arguments.
q.mbti.16p.004: Your living and working spaces are clean and organized.
q.mbti.16p.005: You usually stay calm, even under a lot of pressure.
q.mbti.16p.006: You find the idea of networking or promoting yourself to strangers very daunting.
q.mbti.16p.007: You prioritize and plan tasks effectively, often completing them well before the deadline.
q.mbti.16p.008: People’s stories and emotions speak louder to you than numbers or data.
q.mbti.16p.009: You like to use organizing tools like schedules and lists.
q.mbti.16p.010: Even a small mistake can cause you to doubt your overall abilities and knowledge.
q.mbti.16p.011: You feel comfortable just walking up to someone you find interesting and striking up a conversation.
q.mbti.16p.012: You are not too interested in discussions about various interpretations of creative works.
q.mbti.16p.013: You prioritize facts over people’s feelings when determining a course of action.
q.mbti.16p.014: You often allow the day to unfold without any schedule at all.
q.mbti.16p.015: You rarely worry about whether you make a good impression on people you meet.
q.mbti.16p.016: You enjoy participating in team-based activities.
q.mbti.16p.017: You enjoy experimenting with new and untested approaches.
q.mbti.16p.018: You prioritize being sensitive over being completely honest.
q.mbti.16p.019: You actively seek out new experiences and knowledge areas to explore.
q.mbti.16p.020: You are prone to worrying that things will take a turn for the worse.
q.mbti.16p.021: You enjoy solitary hobbies or activities more than group ones.
q.mbti.16p.022: You cannot imagine yourself writing fictional stories for a living.
q.mbti.16p.023: You favor efficiency in decisions, even if it means disregarding some emotional aspects.
q.mbti.16p.024: You prefer to do your chores before allowing yourself to relax.
q.mbti.16p.025: In disagreements, you prioritize proving your point over preserving the feelings of others.
q.mbti.16p.026: You usually wait for others to introduce themselves first at social gatherings.
q.mbti.16p.027: Your mood can change very quickly.
q.mbti.16p.028: You are not easily swayed by emotional arguments.
q.mbti.16p.029: You often end up doing things at the last possible moment.
q.mbti.16p.031: You usually prefer to be around others rather than on your own.
q.mbti.16p.032: You become bored or lose interest when the discussion gets highly theoretical.
q.mbti.16p.033: When facts and feelings conflict, you usually find yourself following your heart.
q.mbti.16p.034: You find it challenging to maintain a consistent work or study schedule.
q.mbti.16p.035: You rarely second-guess the choices that you have made.
q.mbti.16p.036: Your friends would describe you as lively and outgoing.
q.mbti.16p.037: You are drawn to various forms of creative expression, such as writing.
q.mbti.16p.038: You usually base your choices on objective facts rather than emotional impressions.
q.mbti.16p.039: You like to have a to-do list for each day.
q.mbti.16p.042: You enjoy exploring unfamiliar ideas and viewpoints.
q.mbti.16p.043: You can easily connect with people you have just met.
q.mbti.16p.044: If your plans are interrupted, your top priority is to get back on track as soon as possible.
q.mbti.16p.045: You are still bothered by mistakes that you made a long time ago.
q.mbti.16p.046: You are not too interested in discussing theories on what the world could look like in the future.
q.mbti.16p.047: Your emotions control you more than you control them.
q.mbti.16p.048: When making decisions, you focus more on how the affected people might feel than on what is most logical or efficient.
q.mbti.16p.049: Your personal work style is closer to spontaneous bursts of energy than organized and consistent efforts.
q.mbti.16p.050: When someone thinks highly of you, you wonder how long it will take them to feel disappointed in you.
q.mbti.16p.051: You would love a job that requires you to work alone most of the time.
q.mbti.16p.052: You believe that pondering abstract philosophical questions is a waste of time.
q.mbti.16p.053: You feel more drawn to busy, bustling atmospheres than to quiet, intimate places.
q.mbti.16p.054: If a decision feels right to you, you often act on it without needing further proof.
q.mbti.16p.056: You complete things methodically without skipping over any steps.
q.mbti.16p.057: You prefer tasks that require you to come up with creative solutions rather than follow concrete steps.
q.mbti.16p.058: You are more likely to rely on emotional intuition than logical reasoning when making a choice.
q.mbti.16p.060: You feel confident that things will work out for you.
